findings.title: Async legacy writes derive timeout context from cancelled request context
findings.body: Create, Delete (line 110), Update (line 135) and DeleteCollection (line 163) start goroutines with context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...) where ctx is the incoming request context. The API server cancels that context as soon as the handler returns, which happens immediately after the goroutine is spawned, so the legacy write will almost always run with an already-cancelled context and fail/be aborted. The legacy store therefore silently diverges from unified storage, defeating the stated purpose of mode 3. The goroutine needs a detached context (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a background context preserving values) before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Legacy Create receives the pre-create object instead of the object created in unified storage
findings.body: Storage.Create returns 'created', which carries server-assigned name (generateName), UID, resourceVersion and creationTimestamp, but the goroutine passes the original input 'obj' to Legacy.Create. If the storage does not mutate 'obj' in place, legacy creates a different object (different generated name/UID) or rejects it, so the two stores hold divergent copies. It also races with the caller/storage continuing to use 'obj' after Create returns. The legacy call should use the object returned by unified storage (as the previous synchronous implementation effectively did).

findings.title: Legacy Update reuses the same UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the unified-storage result
findings.body: The previous implementation wrapped objInfo so Legacy.Update received the exact object produced and stored by unified storage. The new code passes the raw objInfo to both Storage.Update and, asynchronously, Legacy.Update, so UpdatedObject is evaluated a second time against the legacy store's old object. If the legacy copy is missing or stale (the normal case while mode 3 is being rolled out, or after a failed async create), the legacy update computes from the wrong base, fails on resourceVersion, or creates/updates divergent content. It also shares objInfo with a goroutine that outlives the request. The result 'res' from Storage.Update should be wrapped (updateWrapper) and passed to legacy, as before.

findings.title: Async legacy failures are never logged
findings.body: In Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection the goroutine only records a duration metric and discards the legacy error; the previous synchronous code logged legacy failures with the object context. Combined with the fire-and-forget design, a permanently failing legacy write (bad object, missing row, timeout) is invisible in logs and unrecoverable, so operators cannot detect or reconcile divergence between unified and legacy storage. Each goroutine should log the error (with kind/name) in addition to recording the metric.

findings.title: Storage failures are recorded as legacy metrics in Create and Update
findings.body: When Storage.Create fails, line 45 calls recordLegacyDuration, and when Storage.Update fails, line 129 does the same, even though legacy was never called and 'startStorage' measured the storage attempt. Storage error rates/latencies for create and update will be invisible while legacy metrics show phantom failures, misleading the dashboards used to judge dual-write health. These should call recordStorageDuration(true, ...).

findings.title: Delete and DeleteCollection record metrics with wrong labels/recorder
findings.body: Delete's success path calls recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...) passing the object name where every other call passes options.Kind, creating per-object-name time series (unbounded cardinality) and breaking kind-based aggregation. DeleteCollection's legacy goroutine at line 166 calls recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, so legacy delete-collection latency/errors are attributed to unified storage. Both misreport the metrics this PR relies on to observe async legacy writes.

findings.title: Mode 3 tests never verify the asynchronous legacy writes
findings.body: TestMode3_Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection return as soon as the unified-storage call succeeds and never wait for or assert on the spawned legacy goroutine (no AssertCalled/waitgroup/synchronisation); several cases don't even register a legacy expectation. The core new behaviour of mode 3 — that legacy is written, with the right object, after unified storage — is therefore untested, and the un-awaited goroutines can also race with subsequent subtests sharing the package-level mocks/fixtures (mock.Mock is not safe for unsynchronised concurrent use). Tests should synchronise on the legacy call and assert its arguments, including that legacy failures do not fail the request.
